en: Udāna 7.2 The Second Discourse on Bhaddiya the Dwarf Thus have I heard:
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the Venerable Sāriputta, considering the Venerable Lakuṇḍaka Bhaddiya to be still a trainee,
instructed, exhorted, inspired, and gladdened him with a Dhamma talk in many ways to an even greater degree.
The Blessed One saw the Venerable Sāriputta instructing, exhorting, inspiring, and gladdening the Venerable Lakuṇḍaka Bhaddiya—
who he considered to be still a trainee— with a discourse on the Dhamma in many ways to an even greater degree.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation (udāna):
“The cycle has been shattered; it has gone beyond hope.
The dried-up stream no longer flows.
The cycle is cut off; it does not turn again.”
“This itself is the end of suffering.
